title: Contrastive QA degradation audit — low-precision variants
content:
Purpose:
This note documents a targeted audit of degradation modes observed when running a contrastive QA benchmark across several low-precision variants (per-channel INT8, symmetric INT8, GPTQ-int4, AWQ-int4). The focus: identify per-question-type failure patterns, actionable thresholds for automatic fallback, and short-term mitigations to protect customer-facing question-answering flows.

High-level summary:
- Dataset: 8k held-out contrastive QA items derived from internal retrieval + user-support logs (balanced across short factual, multi-hop, extractive-paraphrase, and conversational follow-ups).
- Models compared: fp16 baseline (production candidate v2.1), per-channel INT8, symmetric INT8, GPTQ-int4, AWQ-int4. All models are otherwise identical weights-wise; quantization done with our standard toolchain and knob set.
- Primary metrics: Exact Match (EM), F1, top-1 contrastive rank drop (mean), and hallucination incidence (heuristic). Also tracked calibration changes (softmax entropy on answer span).

Key numeric deltas vs fp16 baseline (aggregated):
- per-channel INT8: EM -1.8%, F1 -1.1%, rank drop +0.5
- symmetric INT8: EM -3.5%, F1 -2.9%, rank drop +1.2
- GPTQ-int4: EM -6.7%, F1 -5.8%, rank drop +2.6
- AWQ-int4: EM -4.9%, F1 -4.1%, rank drop +1.8
Note: hallucinatory answers increased notably for GPTQ-int4 (+3.2% absolute) and AWQ-int4 (+1.6% absolute).

Per-question-type breakdown (representative slices):
1) Short factual (single-span retrieval) — 35% of dataset
   - per-channel INT8: EM -0.6%
   - symmetric INT8: EM -1.5%
   - GPTQ-int4: EM -3.2% — errors mostly minor truncations or preposition swaps
   - AWQ-int4: EM -2.2%
   Observations: short spans are generally robust; INT8 variants safe for most traffic.

2) Multi-hop reasoning (explicit chaining) — 18%
   - per-channel INT8: EM -3.9%
   - symmetric INT8: EM -6.2%
   - GPTQ-int4: EM -12.4% — large coherence breakdowns, missing intermediate facts
   - AWQ-int4: EM -9.1%
   Observations: quantization amplifies stepwise error accumulation; GPTQ-int4 shows frequent logical jumps.

3) Paraphrase/extractive (answer requires paraphrase alignment) — 20%
   - per-channel INT8: EM -2.2%
   - symmetric INT8: EM -4.5%
   - GPTQ-int4: EM -7.8%
   - AWQ-int4: EM -5.9%
   Observations: surface-form sensitivity grows with lower precision; F1 loss exceeds EM loss because span boundaries move.

4) Conversational follow-ups (ellipses, referents) — 12%
   - per-channel INT8: EM -2.7%
   - symmetric INT8: EM -5.5%
   - GPTQ-int4: EM -10.9%
   - AWQ-int4: EM -8.6%
   Observations: referent resolution degrades; chain-of-thought implicit signals appear attenuated in int4 runs.

5) Long-context / document-level (>= 2k tokens) — 10%
   - per-channel INT8: EM -1.4%
   - symmetric INT8: EM -2.8%
   - GPTQ-int4: EM -6.0%
   - AWQ-int4: EM -4.7%
   Observations: KV-cache behavior and attention kernel numerical drift may explain some deltas; seen increased token-level omissions.

6) Numeric/math table lookups — 5%
   - GPTQ-int4 shows outlier numeric rounding or sign flips in ~0.7% of items (important for finance/legal slices).

Qualitative failure modes (examples sanitized):
- Missing intermediate fact: Q: "Which third-party shipped the fix before 2021?" FP16 answer: "Acme Corp." GPTQ-int4: "the vendor" (non-specific, lower utility).
- Hallucinated entity: Q: "What is the model ID for the support ticket?" FP16: "ticket_8341" GPTQ-int4: "ticket_8431" (fabricated ID).
- Paraphrase boundary shift: Q requires exact span; int4 outputs include extra adjacent tokens, harming EM though F1 less affected.

Calibration and confidence signals:
- Softmax entropy increases on average for int4 variants (GPTQ-int4 +18% entropy), but model confidence is not reliably correlated with correctness for hallucinations.
- A simple confidence threshold tuned on per-channel INT8 fails to catch ~60% of GPTQ-int4 hallucinations.

Operational impact and risk tiers:
- Low-risk: short factual lookups — safe to route to per-channel INT8 in prod (recommended default for cost-sensitive routes).
- Medium-risk: long-context and paraphrase-heavy queries — recommend symmetric INT8 or per-channel INT8 with monitoring; avoid int4 without fallback.
- High-risk: multi-hop reasoning, conversational follow-ups, numeric/financial queries — do NOT serve from int4 variants behind mission-critical paths. Use fp16 or dedicated INT8 and gating policies.

Recommended rollout controls (short-term):
1) Per-route quantization policy: allow per-route config that pins quantization level (fp16/int8/int4) with explicit risk label. Implement in routing layer and Redwood Console.
2) Canary by slice: run live A/B with per-slice scaffolding (mirror responses; only serve fp16 but log int4 predictions and compare). Use this to detect regressions pre-serve.
3) Confidence + ensemble fallback: if int4 model returns high-entropy or low-contrastive-score response OR fails rank threshold, re-query fp16 and prefer fp16 when disagreement is above threshold.
4) Numeric-safety guard: for any question classified as numeric/financial/legal, force fp16. Classification model provided (small classifier) with ~92% recall on labeled slices.
5) KV-cache warm start: for long-context scenarios, warm / prime the cache with the first pass in fp16 for the first N tokens, then switch to INT8 for continuation — exploratory but promising in internal sim.

Short experiments to run (next 3 weeks):
- Tune AWQ quant params (block size / outlier detection) on multi-hop subset; measure whether coherence improves without large quality loss elsewhere.
- Evaluate mixed-precision decode: compute attention/FFN in INT8 but final layers in fp16. Prototype in serving-runtime branch.
- Retrain or fine-tune small adapter for post-quantization calibration focusing on paraphrase boundaries.

Notes on tooling and reproducibility:
- All runs recorded in eval-hub (confluence link above) and stored under s3://redwood-evals/contrastive-qa/low-precision/2025-01. Configs: quant-configs/*.yaml and seed manifests included in the linked GitHub PR.
- Random seeds used: 42, 73, 101 (triplicate runs to estimate variance).

Open questions / decisions needed:
- What threshold of EM/F1 delta is acceptable per-route for enabling int4 (product decision). Suggested starting point: EM delta <= 2% and hallucination +abs <= 1% for low-risk routes.
- Do we expose a per-customer toggle for quantization level in Dedicated/private deployments? Operational cost/SLAs discussion needed with Product.

Appendix: quick checklist for Solutions/SE teams when proposing int4 pilots:
- Provide a short list of representative prompts (20–50) from customer workload across identified slices.
- Run mirrored int4 and fp16 in staging; collect contrastive rank and hallucination heuristics.
- If numeric/legal content present >2% traffic, block int4 by default.
- Include fallback policy in deployment manifest (canary, rollback SLO).

Author notes / informal:
- Diego ran extra runs where we clipped layernorm scales — that reduced GPTQ-int4 hallucinations slightly; unclear whether generalizable.
- Priya observed that aggressive LR during calibration pass for GPTQ led to brittle behavior; be conservative with calibration optimizers.
- Connor is prototyping the mixed-precision prototype in branch `mixed-quant-probe` (PR linked).

Conclusion:
Int8 per-channel offers a strong cost/quality win and is a reasonable first step for many contrastive-qa routes. GPTQ-int4 shows sharper degradation and an elevated hallucination risk; AWQ-int4 sits in between but still risky for multi-hop and conversational slices. Short-term mitigations (per-route policies, ensemble fallback, numeric-guards) reduce risk sufficiently to enable cautious pilots, but int4 should not be blanket-enabled on high-risk paths without additional safeguards.

-- End of audit note --
